incidents.victim: Bulgarian state administration networks
incidents.vector: Long-dwelling intrusion across fragmented government networks lacking centralized monitoring; exact initial entry vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Group had access for at least five years and exfiltrated tens of millions of government documents before being evicted.

incidents.victim: FBI — National Crime Information Center (NCIC)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the bureau's second breach this year after a September intrusion into its HR portal.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained access to the database used for warrants, fugitive tracking, and background checks; scope of data exposure not yet disclosed.

incidents.victim: Austrian Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs (MOFA)
incidents.vector: Hackers believed to have entered through a third-party provider running the ministry's official website.
incidents.impact: Staff data was stolen; attribution and full scope not yet confirmed.

incidents.victim: Tigerfish (audio/video transcription service)
incidents.vector: Customer data was left exposed online rather than actively stolen; discovered by security researchers.
incidents.impact: Exposed transcriptions included law enforcement body camera footage transcripts.

incidents.victim: JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard (via shared third-party provider)
incidents.vector: Data-extortion group n0n claimed the attack; the companies confirmed limited data was stolen from a shared third-party provider.
incidents.impact: Limited customer/operational data exposed across three major financial institutions; full scope not disclosed.

incidents.victim: Rackspace Spot (cloud marketplace)
incidents.vector: Attackers used authentic credentials leaked by a third party to access the Rackspace Spot marketplace.
incidents.impact: Intruders stole Kubernetes secrets from customer accounts and deployed their own pods using the stolen access.

incidents.victim: 40+ Irish and UK credit unions (via software supplier Wellington IT)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in systems run by software supplier Wellington IT, which processes mobile banking app data for credit unions.
incidents.impact: Payment details of credit union members were accessed; the breach went unnoticed for roughly six weeks before affected credit unions were notified.

incidents.victim: Iceland's largest web hosting provider (1984 Hosting)
incidents.vector: Hosting provider says an AI-assisted attacker breached its systems rapidly, prompting an emergency shutdown of services.
incidents.impact: Tens of thousands of customer websites were taken offline, including services relied on by dissidents worldwide.

incidents.victim: Universities in East Asia (two institutions, unnamed)
incidents.vector: Operator directed the autonomous AI penetration-testing tool Cairn against target IP addresses; the AI agents discovered and exploited an unpatched zero-day path-traversal flaw in an open-source medical imaging application.
incidents.impact: Attacker gained access to two university networks using the same zero-day; Amazon worked with the open-source maintainers to patch the flaw and notified the affected organizations via a government partner.

incidents.victim: Financial services, healthcare, and legal organizations (multiple, unnamed; US, UK, Australia)
incidents.vector: Attackers impersonate internal IT support via vishing calls, directing employees to adversary-in-the-middle proxy pages that relay credentials and MFA approvals in real time.
incidents.impact: Multiple waves of data theft and extortion across data-rich industries; newly identified clusters are expanding targeting into healthcare and pharmaceutical organizations.

incidents.victim: Portugal's Institute for Mobility and Transport (IMT)
incidents.vector: Multiple cyberattacks against the transportation agency, part of a wider wave hitting Portuguese government bodies in recent weeks.
incidents.impact: IMT suspended all services as a precaution; no evidence of data theft reported. It is the fourth Portuguese government body targeted recently.

incidents.victim: Unibet and affiliated online casinos (FDJ United)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack against FDJ United's sports betting and casino platforms; nature of the attack not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Unibet and several online casino sites were taken offline.

incidents.victim: GL.iNet (travel routers and IP KVM devices)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-management service to push backdoors to connected devices.
incidents.impact: Some travel routers and IP KVM devices were backdoored; GL.iNet blocked the attack path and released firmware fixes, recommending factory resets for already-infected devices.

incidents.victim: Ransomware-attack victims defrauded via RansomwareHelp
incidents.vector: RansomwareHelp's CTO secretly paid ransomware operators for decryption keys while publicly claiming proprietary cryptographic recovery, then charged victims steep markups.
incidents.impact: An FBI sting found the firm charged a fake victim $16,010 for a decryptor it bought for about $6,000; a real client was separately quoted $438,880 for the same service. The CTO was indicted for wire fraud.

incidents.victim: VMware vCenter Server deployments (multiple organizations, unnamed)
incidents.vector: Suspected PRC-nexus actor exploited a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764), then pivoted internally and exploited a second vCenter zero-day (CVE-2026-123890) with custom malware to bypass authentication.
incidents.impact: Attacker gained administrator-level access to vCenter, exfiltrated directory-service databases, hijacked the SSO token service, and created persistent admin accounts for continued access.

incidents.victim: Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage)
incidents.vector: Underlying 2023 Mr. Cooper breach involved attackers impersonating employees by phone to obtain temporary passwords from the IT help desk, bypassing MFA; Rocket Mortgage separately failed to report incidents promptly or implement MFA.
incidents.impact: NYDFS fined Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper a combined $6.75 million for Cybersecurity Regulation violations, including late incident reporting and inadequate authentication controls.

incidents.victim: Americans and Europeans targeted by Southeast Asia-based crypto investment scam centers
incidents.vector: OFAC sanctioned scam-compound operators and an armed group (DKBA) providing protection and oversight for scam centers running virtual-currency investment fraud.
incidents.impact: Sanctions target scam-center operators and facilitators tied to forced-labor scam compounds on the Thai-Myanmar border, part of a broader U.S. effort to disrupt cyber-enabled fraud networks.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Entra ID customers (multiple tenants)
incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a bug in the Entra Connect Health API, introduced by a July update, to scrape tenant configuration data.
incidents.impact: Attacker collected administrator email addresses and general tenant configuration data across affected customers; Microsoft deployed a fix.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders, gaming platform users, and VoIP software users (Europe-focused)
incidents.vector: Trojanized installers and lure documents (fake financial statements, messaging/VoIP app installers) delivered a remote access trojan, an infostealer, and a cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker.
incidents.impact: Victims' credentials, files, and cryptocurrency were targeted; the actor used Solana blockchain transactions to host resilient command-and-control infrastructure.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations using Optimizely Web Experimentation
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into the custom code field of customer accounts.
incidents.impact: Malicious code was served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN to visitors of at least 178 customer websites, swapping cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimming payment cards, and attempting to deliver mobile exploit kits; at least $7,000 in cryptocurrency was confirmed stolen.

incidents.victim: DonorPerfect (fundraising platform)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack prompted the company to take its systems offline; specific vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Systems were taken offline and are being slowly restored; unclear whether customer or donor data was stolen.

incidents.victim: The Container Store
incidents.vector: Cybercriminal group n0n claimed the attack and listed the company on its data-leak site; specific intrusion vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Online ordering and in-store transaction systems were disrupted; the company says there is no evidence yet that customer financial data was stolen, though the leak-site claims remain unaddressed.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Agriculture
incidents.vector: Security team discovered a breach affecting applications used to issue payments to American farmers.
incidents.impact: Payment applications were taken offline for over a week; the agency reset passwords across all databases as a precaution.

incidents.victim: Nissan (dealer repair IT platform)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on an IT platform used by repair shops, initially mistaken for a routine technical outage.
incidents.impact: Repair shops have been unable to diagnose vehicles, ship fixes and firmware updates, or replace lost key fobs since Nov. 13.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor, defense, and civil-society organizations (19 targeted, 10 compromised; unnamed)
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers paired the open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn with Chinese AI models (Zhipu GLM, DeepSeek) to run 25 largely autonomous intrusion operations.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained unauthorized access or data at 10 organizations, including more than one million exposed personal records at one organization, military/government identities, and a modified industry-standards ballot document.

incidents.victim: Japan Digital Agency
incidents.vector: Files from the agency's file-sharing service were left exposed online rather than stolen through active exploitation.
incidents.impact: Files were publicly accessible for roughly three and a half months, from July 30 to November 12, 2026.

incidents.victim: Vanderbilt University
incidents.vector: Ransomware group BYOD gained access to university systems, prompting a shutdown of devices and Wi-Fi during containment.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen more than one million Social Security numbers; multiple campus IT services were disrupted for days. BYOD has also hit other academic and healthcare targets.
